content.title: 2026 Oscars Winners List: Full Results From the Academy Awards
content.text: Skip to main content Oscars: ‘One Battle After Another’ Takes Best Picture, Director & Four Others; Jordan & Buckley Win Lead Acting Prizes: Full List The cast and creators of 'One Battle After Another' onstage after the pic's Best Picture Scar won Getty Images Warner Bros’ action comedy One Battle After Another was named Best Picture at the 98th annual Academy Awards, which were handed out Sunday night at the Dolby Theater in Hollywood. See the full list below, followed by charts noting wins by film and by studio. RELATED: All The Best Picture Oscar Winners – Photo Gallery RELATED: Oscars TV Review: Hollywood’s Big Night Finally Gets As Big As The Movies it Celebrates One Battle After Another scored a leading six wins, and WB’s Depression-era genre smash Sinners was next with four, ending a marathon awards season in which the studio mates battled each other for months. Amid the studio’s $110 billion acquisition by Paramount Skydance, Warner Bros led distributors with 11 statuettes. Netflix was next with seven, including three for Frankenstein. The streamer’s KPop Demon Hunters was the only other film to score multiple trophies Sunday, and no other studio got more than one. RELATED: The Oscars: Best Looks From The Red Carpet RELATED: Oscars 2026: The Biggest Moments You Didn’t See On TV RELATED: Oscars Analysis: In Changing Times This Was A Night Of Triumph For Original Filmmaking, Warner Bros, And A Hollywood On Edge Michael B. Jordan won the contentious Best Actor race for his dual role as Smoke and Stack in Sinners, following up his triumph at the Actor Awards two weeks ago. It was his first career Academy Award nomination. Read more on his win from Deadline’s Baz Bamigboye here. RELATED: All The Best Actor Oscar Winners – Photo Gallery Jessie Buckley then surprised no one with her Best Actress win for Focus Features’ Hamnet. She picked up her first career Oscar on her first nom and became the first Irishwoman to win the prize, after steamrolling through awards season for her aching portrayal of William Shakespeare’s partner Agnes. RELATED: All The Best Actress Oscar Winners – Photo Gallery Paul Thomas Anderson took the statuette for Best Directing after winning earlier for Best Adapted Screenplay for One Battle After Another — his first Academy Awards after 11 previous nominations dating to 1998. He became just the ninth person to win Best Picture, Directing and Screenplay Oscars on the same night. RELATED: Oscars 2026: What You Didn’t See On TV Ryan Coogler followed with his first Oscar triumph, taking Original Screenplay for Sinners. It was his fifth career nomination. Anderson and Coogler also claimed the top screenplay prizes at the Writers Guild Awards. You can read the Sinners screenplay here. RELATED: All The Best Director Oscar Winners – Photo Gallery One Battle After Another‘s Sean Penn won Best Supporting Actor, following up his win at the Actor Awards this month. It’s his third career Oscar but first in the category. He also has three other noms for Lead Actor. Penn wasn’t at the ceremony to accept his prize. RELATED: All The Best Supporting Actor Oscar Winners – Photo Gallery After host Conan O’Brien’s monologue, Amy Madigan took home the first prize of the night, winning Best Supporting Actress for her role as creepy Aunt Gladys in Warner Bros’ Weapons. She was a favorite after winning at the Critics Choice and Actor Awards. Madigan also noted being a Supporting Actress Oscar nominee back in 1986 for Twice in a Life. Watch a video interview with Madigan here. RELATED: All The Best Supporting Actress Oscar Winners – Photo Gallery The inaugural Oscar for Best Casting went to Cassandra Kulukundis of for One Battle After Another, who thanked those who “fought tirelessly” to get the category added. It was something of an upset in that the film was shut out at Casting Society’s Artios Awards in late February. The category’s nominees were announced one by one, honoring the award’s historic debut at the Academy Awards. RELATED: Movies That Should Have Won The Best Picture Oscar – Photo Gallery Netflix’s Frankenstein took three wins for craft awards, including two back-to-back for Best Makeup & Hairstyling and Best Costume Design. Guillermo del Toro‘s pic later won the statuette for Production Design. It also was a winner at the Make-Up Artists and Hair Stylists Guild Awards last month, taking that prize for Best Special Make-Up Prosthetics in Make-Up/Hairstyling. It also won for Excellence in Period Film at the CDGA and for Period Feature Film at the Art Directors Guild Awards. Watch a video interview with del Toro here. RELATED: Snubs And Surprises At The 2026 Oscars: From Live-Action Short Film Tie To Films Leaving Empty-Handed Also on the crafts front, Apple Original Films’ racing pic F1 took the Best Sound prize, Best Editing went to One Battle After Another, and Sinners won Best Cinematography. One Battle also was a winner at this year’s ACE Eddie Awards and ASC Awards. F1 took the checkered flag twice at Cinema Audio Society’s CAS Awards. RELATED: All The Best International Feature Film Oscar Winners – Photo Gallery Norway picked up its first Academy Award ever with the Best International Feature win for Neon’s Cannes-debuting Sentimental Value. It also was up for Best Picture tonight. Javier Bardem presented the award, after he said “No to war, and free Palestine” onstage. RELATED: The 60 Movies That Have Made More Than $1 Billion At The Global Box Office KPop Demon Hunters, Netflix’s most popular film ever, won the golden statuette for Best Animated Feature. The film produced by Sony Pictures Animation swept the Annie Awards last month, going 10-for-10 in its nominated categories. It has been streamed more than 500 million times, and its soundtrack has been streamed more than 11 billion times (with a capital B). See a gallery of the 25 highest-grossing animated movies of all time here. RELATED: All The Best Animated Feature Oscar Winners – Photo Gallery The pic later surprised no one by winning Best Song for the Grammy-winning international pop smash “Golden.” It’s the first tune from the K-pop genre to pick up an Oscar. That left Diane Warren with a record 17 career Oscar nominations without a win. She did pick up an Honorary Oscar at the 2022 Governor Awards, though. 20th Century Studios’ billion-dollar threequel Avatar: Fire and Ash won Best Visual Effects. It’s a sucker bet to pick against a pic in James Cameron’s historic franchise, which has taken FX Oscars for the original in 2010 and Avatar: The Way of Water in 2023. Fire and Ash dominated the VES Awards with seven wins last month. RELATED: All 21 EGOT Winners From Rita Moreno to Whoopi Goldberg – Photo Gallery In a major shocker, the Documentary Feature Oscar went to Mr. Nobody Against Putin, the Kino Lorber-distributed film that was Denmark’s entry for Best International Feature Film. The movie scooped the World Cinema Documentary Special Jury Award at Sundance last year, but the category was expected to be a race between favorites The Perfect Neighbor and Come See Me in the Good Light. The Girl Who Cried Pearls got the win for Best Animated Short. Colm Feore narrates English-language version of the pic that debuted at last year’s Annecy International Film Festival. Later, The Singers (Netflix) and Two People Exchanging Saliva (Canal+/The New Yorker) both won for Live Action Short in only the seventh tie in Oscars history. All the Empty Rooms, about the fallout of school shootings, later won the Documentary Short prize. RELATED: Where To Watch The 2026 Oscar Contenders, From ‘Sinners’ To ‘Sentimental Value’ Ludwig Göransson won his third career Oscar, Best Score for Sinners. He also was a winner at the Society of Composers and Lyricists’ SOC Awards. The Black Panther and Oppenheimer composer paid loving tribute to his father during his acceptance speech. Billy Crystal began the lengthy In Memoriam segment with a tribute to his “best friend” Rob Reiner, who was killed along with his wife Michele in their home last year. Barbra Streisand paid heartfelt tribute to her late The Way We Were co-star Robert Redford and then sang a passage from its Oscar-winning theme song. There was a separate tribute to four female screen legends: Claudia Cardinale, Diane Ladd, Catherine O’Hara and Diane Keaton.
